items.title: v2.1.185
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[v2.1.185](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.185)** — _Claude Code releases_. — Stream-stall timeout doubled from 10s to 20s and the hint reworded from No response from API · Retrying in … to Waiting for API response · will retry in … — a UX polish, no behavioural change to retry logic.

score_components.taste_reason: Trivial release: just a UI hint string change and 10s→20s timeout bump. Technically new since state-of-ai's v2.1.157 but too minor to stop for.

items.title: Beyond LoRA: Can you beat the most popular fine-tuning technique?
items.bullet_md: - 🟡 **[Beyond LoRA: Can you beat the most popular fine-tuning technique?](https://huggingface.co/blog/peft-beyond-lora)** — _Hugging Face blog_. — Hugging Face benchmarked six PEFT methods on equal footing and found LoRA sits below the Pareto frontier on image generation — OFT scored 0.708 vs LoRA's 0.697 on dino similarity while using 9.01 GB of VRAM against LoRA's 9.97 GB — and switching techniques in the PEFT library is a one-line config change.

score_components.taste_reason: Expected exploration of PEFT methods beyond LoRA; solid educational content but no surprising findings or new benchmarks.

items.title: New GLM 5.2 Model - 1M Tokens, Open Weights & 5X Cheaper Than Opus
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [New GLM 5.2 Model - 1M Tokens, Open Weights & 5X Cheaper Than Opus](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3RKnZDf8v3c) — **Pure AI Solutions** (2m11s). — A rundown of Z.ai's GLM-5.2 release covering its 744B-parameter MoE architecture, IndexShare attention that cuts per-token FLOPs by 2.9× at 1M context, and MIT-licensed weights — useful if you are evaluating open-weight alternatives to Claude or GPT for long-horizon coding tasks.

score_components.taste_reason: Extends state-of-ai's GLM-5.1 row with 5.2's 1M-token context and cost-efficiency claim (5x cheaper than Opus). Concrete specs but from a generic YouTube channel with thin analysis.

items.title: This Claude Code Plugin Writes 94% Less Code (ponytail)
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [This Claude Code Plugin Writes 94% Less Code (ponytail)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xuFcmUAQUc) — **Better Stack** (10m07s). — A walkthrough of Ponytail — DietrichGebert's open-source skill that installs across 14 agent platforms and enforces a six-rung laziness ladder before writing code, averaging 54% less code (up to 94% on overbuilt tasks like date pickers) while keeping full safety on adversarial tests.

score_components.taste_reason: Interesting Claude Code plugin demo but the '94% less code' claim sounds exaggerated; useful enough for a quick watch.

items.title: How To Build Beautiful Apps FAST - Without a Designer (Claude Code & Codex + Mobbin MCP)

score_components.taste_reason: Practical tutorial on using Mobbin MCP with Claude Code for UI prototyping; useful for frontend-focused devs but not surprising.

items.title: Build a "Code Mode" MCP Server in Elixir
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Build a "Code Mode" MCP Server in Elixir](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xejfNsxjK3o) — **Code and Stuff** (21m10s). — A tutorial on setting up an MCP server in Elixir using AshAi, covering the Streamable HTTP transport, JSON-RPC message handling, and session management via GenServer — relevant if you run Elixir/Phoenix in production and want to expose domain tools to Claude Code.

score_components.taste_reason: Elixir Ash ecosystem adding OAuth 2 + MCP + Lua scripting is technically interesting MCP infrastructure work but very language-specific; most readers skim past.

items.title: GLM 5.2 SUPER MODE: Here's HOW TO USE GLM-5.2 to it's FULL POTENTIAL
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [GLM 5.2 SUPER MODE: Here's HOW TO USE GLM-5.2 to it's FULL POTENTIAL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n3AMXRct2nc) — **AICodeKing** (9m04s). — A walkthrough of using GLM-5.2 with Verdent to scaffold a full-stack creator sponsorship dashboard from a single prompt — useful for evaluating how the model handles agentic multi-file generation at its Max thinking effort level.

score_components.taste_reason: Clickbait title with ALL CAPS penalties the content before reading — a sponsorship dashboard tutorial using GLM-5.2 is too niche to justify the framing.

items.title: Is AI Coding Making Developers Dumber?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Is AI Coding Making Developers Dumber?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CaXENGk5e-0) — **Devsplainers** (9m43s). — A rundown of Anthropic's randomized controlled trial where developers using AI scored 17% lower on a post-task quiz about a new Python library, with the sharpest drop in debugging skills — but those who asked conceptual questions rather than just delegating code generation retained normal scores.

score_components.taste_reason: Well-worn perennial topic (AI skill atrophy), clickbait title framing, no new research specifics cited in the enriched body. Skim-past.

items.title: What sentiment analysis can't see: Measuring whether customers were helped, and what went wrong, across 70,000 support conversations
items.bullet_md: - 🧪 **[What sentiment analysis can't see: Measuring whether customers were helped, and what went wrong, across 70,000 support conversations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19698)** — _arXiv cs.CL_. — A study of 70,450 support conversations found GPT-5.4 satisfaction estimates tracked user ratings at 0.47 correlation vs sentiment's 0.36, with tone and satisfaction disagreeing in 44% of cases and the largest group being tolerated friction — satisfied customers still reporting fixable problems that no sentiment dashboard surfaces.

score_components.taste_reason: Concrete large-scale study (70,450 conversations, GPT-5.4) comparing sentiment analysis vs LLM-based support evaluation. Practical findings but domain-specific to customer support.
